name: Google Photos
description: Google Photos is Google's cloud photo and video service for organizing personal media. Individuals use it to preserve, find, and explicitly select memories across their devices.
agentUseSummary: Connect one Google account through Relay-owned OAuth, then let agents use four bounded Google Photos Picker wrappers to create a user-controlled selection session, inspect one explicit session once, read the first metadata-only page for at most twenty-five selected items, and clean up the session. Relay V1 excludes removed broad Library scopes, whole-library access, uploads, edits, albums, sharing, raw media, base URLs, camera or EXIF data, faces, unrelated ML, advertising, automatic polling, pagination, delegation, and raw tools.

capabilities.label: Read selected metadata

capabilities.description: Create and clean up bounded user-controlled selection sessions.

blocked.description: Removed whole-library, sharing, and broad Library scopes are forbidden.

blocked.label: Upload or edit Library content
blocked.description: Library API uploads, imports, albums, and app-created-data management are outside V1.

blocked.label: Access raw selected media

blocked.label: Search or share Photos Library
blocked.description: Whole-library access, albums, search, and sharing are outside Picker-only V1.

blocked.label: Analyze faces or repurpose Photos data
blocked.description: Face analysis, unrelated ML training, advertising, brokerage, and competing galleries are blocked.

blocked.label: Automatically poll or paginate
blocked.description: Automatic polling and page-token following are blocked in V1.

blocked.label: Run raw or delegated Photos access
blocked.description: Raw endpoints, service accounts, and domain-wide delegation are blocked.

approvalProfiles.label: Safe
approvalProfiles.description: Explicit session checks and first-page metadata reads run automatically; session creation and cleanup require matching approval.

approvalProfiles.label: Dangerously skip permissions
approvalProfiles.description: All four selected tools run without Relay per-action approval while exact Picker scope, user selection, item and page limits, metadata redaction, no-polling, audit, refresh, revocation, and provider limits remain enforced.

runtimeSupport.description: Relay mounts four privacy-bounded Google Photos Picker wrappers and attaches encrypted OAuth tokens server-side.

providerSetup.blocker: Relay must configure its Google Cloud project and confidential web client, enable Photos Picker API, publish its OAuth consent screen with verified relayconsole.work domains, Limited Use disclosure, policy links, and affirmative selection consent, complete Google's applicable verification for the Picker scope, configure Railway staging credentials, and authorize an acceptance account. Those provider-console and environment actions are outside this worker task.
providerSetup.nextAction: In the provider-console task, configure the canonical Railway callback and exact Picker scope, complete Google review, configure staging credentials, then verify all four tools, user-controlled selection, 25-item and one-page bounds, metadata redaction, Safe and Dangerous policy, refresh, rotation, revocation, disconnect, cleanup, quota/error mapping, and post-disconnect denial.

evidence.supports: Google documents PickingSession creation, explicit retrieval, deletion, picker URI, readiness, expiry, bounded configuration, and polling guidance.
Picked media listing requires the exact Picker scope, an explicit session, a bounded page size, and optional pagination; Relay reads one page only.
PickedMediaItem includes media metadata and a raw-content base URL; Relay returns only bounded metadata and strips base URLs and camera details.
Google removed broad Library read and sharing scopes after March 31, 2025 and directs whole-library selection to Picker API.

Google requires minimum contextual permissions, transparent disclosure, affirmative consent, Limited Use compliance, and prohibits advertising, brokerage, competing galleries, faces, and unrelated ML uses.
